topics.topic: Startup cleanup of unreferenced content-addressed value bytes
questions: Does store.open_store remove unreferenced content-addressed value bytes at start, and if not, which operation does?
Must `open_store` also remove unreferenced content-addressed value bytes, and if so when may it read the database to determine references?
Which operation removes unreferenced content-addressed value bytes at startup?

quotes:
On start, temporary files,
   value bytes no record names (left by a failed call, so only trial fixtures
   and named values outlive a run, K-10; owner, 2026-10-07) and
   the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool (A14) are
   removed; nothing else is.

The store's own temporary files — those it writes before a rename (A18 rule 4)
— are removed, and nothing else is;
judgement.why: State 2 requires removal of unnamed value files, while State 5 says open_store removes only temporary files and nothing else.

topics.topic: Handling corrupt, unreadable, incompatible, or migration-requiring existing stores
questions: What must `open_store` return or do for an unreadable, corrupt or schema-incompatible existing store?
What must `store.open_store` do when the database exists but is corrupt, has an unknown schema version, or requires migration for the running release?

quotes:
the database schema, the
content-addressed area and the spool area are created inside the data
directory when absent.
judgement.why: The reopening change did not touch this passage or make the behavior of an existing corrupt, incompatible, or migration-requiring database newly material.

topics.topic: Valid api_base_url forms, Host authority, and path joining
questions: Are user-info, query, fragment, empty or non-root paths, percent-encoded authority characters and other absolute-URL components permitted in `api_base_url`, and exactly which authority text becomes the Host header?
Which additional `api_base_url` forms are valid, and exactly how are paths joined when the base URL has multiple trailing slashes, a path component, user information, a query, or a fragment?

judgement.why: This is the same api_base_url grammar, authority, loopback-classification, and path-joining question as P1, and neither its passages nor the reopening change altered it.

precedent.topic: Allowed api_base_url syntax, normalization, joining, and loopback classification
quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
precedent.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.

topics.topic: Approval-wait representation and EffectApproval data used by operation_element_conclusion
questions: What does this operation return for an element waiting for owner approval, which by rule has an EffectApproval but no NodeExecution?
Must the operation also read EffectApproval records to distinguish an unreached element from one waiting for approval and to obtain its `approval_id`?

topics.topic: Atomic ordering and preflight requirements for multiple output materialization
questions: In what order are multiple outputs validated, canonicalized, published and spooled, and must all output sizes and spool ceilings be preflighted before any output bytes are written?

topics.topic: Atomicity when a later captured file fails validation
questions: For a capture containing several files, what happens if validation while copying a later file finds a digest or size mismatch after earlier files were published?

topics.topic: Canonical JSON input representation and duplicate-key detection ownership
questions: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text or a parsed representation that preserves duplicate object members, and which module detects duplicate keys?

topics.topic: Classification and size precedence for non-canonical sandbox outputs
questions: How is a returned Python value that cannot be represented as canonical JSON—such as a non-finite float, unsupported object or cyclic structure—classified, and how does `output_bytes` precedence apply when its canonical size cannot be computed?

topics.topic: Eligibility and ordering constraints for rollback targets
questions: Must the target precede the current implementation or activation in store order, or may rollback select any admitted implementation of the current contract version?

topics.topic: Encoding or refusal of header-unsafe multipart port metadata
questions: How are port names and media types containing quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII text or other header-unsafe characters represented or refused when constructing multipart headers?

topics.topic: MCP refusal code for canonicalization failures
questions: What refusal code does the MCP caller receive when canonicalization rejects a non-finite number or duplicate object key?

topics.topic: MCP transport, protocol version, endpoint, and framing exposed by serve_kernel
questions: Which MCP transport and protocol/version does `serve_kernel` implement at the listen address, and what endpoint or framing exposes the catalogue?

topics.topic: Missing-record errors from add_captured_trial_case
questions: What error is returned when the named implementation, contract version, source NodeExecution or referenced SpooledFile does not exist?

topics.topic: Opacity and permitted inspection of prepared requests
questions: Is the prepared request an opaque, single-module-owned value that effects can only pass back to send_prepared_request, or may effects inspect its complete URL, headers and body?

topics.topic: Recovery and retry behavior after an invalid token-list configuration
questions: After a failed re-read clears the token list, must every request retry reading until a valid list is obtained, even when the restored file digest equals the last successful digest?

topics.topic: Required sandbox probe and its success criteria
questions: What exact probe must run, and what observations constitute success rather than merely a Python process returning normally?

topics.topic: Resolution semantics for manifest_revision
questions: How is `manifest_revision` resolved: from a version-control object, a revision-specific directory, or a checkout whose current contents are merely labelled by the configured revision?

topics.topic: Scope of ownership and permission validation when opening a store
questions: Does `open_store` validate ownership and permissions of every existing database, content-area and spool entry, or only the data directory itself?

topics.topic: Startup binding checks, capability scope, ordering, and failure selection
questions: Which exact subset of A08 checks runs at startup, which capabilities are examined, and in what order is the first failure selected?

topics.topic: Supplying and validating authored file-fixture bytes
questions: How do authored input and expected-output file fixtures supply their bytes to `functions.add_trial_case`, and which module computes and verifies their facts?

topics.topic: Unit used for disclosed failure-detail length
questions: What unit is used for the disclosed length of a classified failure detail?

topics.topic: Validation of service identity syntax and responsible startup operation
questions: Are service identities appearing in `service_instances` and `service_credentials` required to match `SERVICE_ID_PATTERN`, and which startup operation refuses an invalid one before it can be used to construct a manifest path?

topics.topic: Whether read operations return full records or declared output subsets
questions: Do these read operations return the complete State 1 record, or exactly the subset named in each operation's Outputs section?

topics.topic: Whether serving continues after an ordinary internal error
questions: After an ordinary `internal_error`, does `surface` terminate the process after answering, or continue serving requests?
